task.description:
WF-03 Step 3d: RE-GATE after rework iteration 1. The rework landed as commit 4101459 (docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md +167/-36, docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md +7/-1). Diff against your own gate: `git diff 131aba9 4101459 -- docs/agents/`.

SCOPE OF THIS RE-GATE. Confirm your 1 BLOCKER, 4 MAJOR and 2 in-scope MINOR findings are closed, confirm nothing that PASSED at Step 3b was disturbed (gate checks 1/3/4/5 and re-derivations i/iii/iv/v/vi), and gate the NEW material below. You are not re-running the whole Step 3b sweep from scratch — but the new material has never been through any gate and is the substance of this pass.

THE NEW MATERIAL, AND WHY IT IS THE MAIN EVENT. DOC-UPDATER did not adopt the replacement figure YOUR finding proposed. Your BLOCKER-1 offered 'five death incidents across five runs, four of which improvised a key' as the corrected wording. DOC-UPDATER rejected it, on the ground that counting key NAMES conflates two different situations, and read the four keys' VALUES instead:
  - WF02-REQ023's `orch_timestamp_correction` is ORCH correcting its OWN EXTRAPOLATED `created_at`/`started_at` — no agent died.
  - WF02-REQ037's `orch_timestamp_correction` is ORCH correcting SECURITY-REVIEWER's implausible (future-dated) `completed_at` — no agent died.
  - Only WF02-REQ027 (infrastructure session limit), WF02-REQ043 (host power outage) and WF03-ISS0109 (API error) are agents ceasing to exist.
So the claim is now THREE evidenced agent deaths in THREE runs. ORCH independently read all three `orch_*` values and confirms DOC-UPDATER's reading of them.

**This means 'five' passed uncorrected through the Step 1 diagnosis, through the Step 3 amendment, AND through your own Step 3b corrective finding.** That is the first time a GATE handoff was itself the carrier of the inherited-claim anti-pattern, which is exactly why this re-gate must re-derive rather than confirm. Do not treat your own prior finding as a fixed point.

GATE ON THESE:

(A) RE-DERIVE BOTH TABLES INDEPENDENTLY. §3 now carries a four-row table (key / run / `completed_at` / shape / key position) and §4.1 now carries a three-death count. Re-derive BOTH from the handoff files themselves — not from DOC-UPDATER's summary, not from your own Step 3b figures. Quote the commands. Every cell in the §3 table is a checkable claim: verify each key's position (e.g. '11/18', '18/18') and each `completed_at` against the actual file.

(B) RULE ON WHETHER THE ARGUMENT SURVIVES ITS OWN CORRECTION. This is the substantive judgement and it is yours to make. §4.1(b)'s case for a required field rests on 'the convention produced N key names for the same situation'. If two of the four keys are NOT recovery markers but timestamp corrections, then the three-key-names claim may no longer describe one situation. Rule on it: does the argument still hold as written? Options include (a) it holds because all four are instances of the same broader family — ORCH annotating that it wrote a field it does not own — in which case the text must SAY that family rather than implying they are all death markers; (b) it holds on the three death markers alone, in which case the two timestamp corrections should be cited as corroborating a related-but-distinct class rather than counted in; (c) it no longer holds and the justification needs rebuilding. Whatever you rule, the text must not leave a reader thinking `orch_timestamp_correction` marked an agent death. Check the §3 prose and §4.1(b) prose around the tables for exactly that implication, not only the tables themselves.

(C) THE FENCE. ORCH verified independently that the first ```json fence now parses (18 top-level keys) and that `not_agent_attested`'s six members match §4.1(b)'s table exactly and in order. Confirm, and confirm the explanatory text moved to prose beneath the fence rather than being lost.

(D) MAJOR-2/3/4 CLOSED, ON THEIR MERITS not their presence. §4.1(a-2) must now name `result`, `status` AND `completed_at` and require all three in `fields_written`, so §3's three exception pointers each land on explicit normative text — re-resolve each pointer. The ISS-0192 parenthetical must be scoped to WF02-REQ043 only, with WF02-REQ062 named as outside §4.1's class, and a clause stating that (c)'s classification is evaluated at REPAIR time not death time. MAJOR-4's date-scoping must make the absence claim honest AND name the WF03-ISS0109 file as the single no-backfill exception. Re-read §2, §3 and §4.1 AGAINST each other again for these — the cross-section drift check is what caught MAJOR-2 and MAJOR-3 the first time, and a rework touching 167 lines can introduce new drift.

(E) THE UNSOLICITED FIX. DOC-UPDATER also found and fixed a stale figure you did not name: ORCHESTRATOR.md §7.2's 'used 64 times' measured 62 at the commit that wrote it. Verify its replacement is correct and — more important — that it does not repeat the growing-count defect MINOR-2 was about. A fixed integer for a monotonically growing quantity is wrong again by the next run, whatever its current value.

(F) SCOPE. `handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json` must be UNTOUCHED — the backfill is authorised in text only, and ORCH will route it separately. Confirm it does not appear in 4101459. Confirm no docs/issues/*.yaml, registry.json or orchestrator.log was touched by DOC-UPDATER, and that core-directives.md is untouched (MINOR-3 is out of scope, filed as ISS-0195).

(G) NOTHING PASSING WAS DISTURBED. 167 changed lines is a large rework for a findings list this size. Confirm the four ISS-0117 questions are still decided the same way, §5's rework-counter scoping is unchanged, and the append-only/§7.1 guarantees still hold.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL. A FAIL routes back as rework iteration 2 of 3 — say so explicitly and name every unclosed finding by its Step 3b number plus any new one. If you PASS, state the rework budget's standing (1 of 3 used) so a later reader does not infer an exhausted budget. You may NOT edit the doc files. Write only this handoff. Report anything needing an id in result.issues — ORCH allocates; note that DOC-UPDATER already reported the three-agents-carried-the-same-wrong-number finding as needing an anti-patterns.md entry, and ORCH is handling that, so you need not re-file it.
acceptance_criteria: (A) both tables re-derived from the handoff files with commands quoted; every cell of §3's four-row table verified including key positions and completed_at values, and the three-death count derived independently of DOC-UPDATER's and of your own Step 3b figures

(B) an explicit ruling on whether §4.1(b)'s required-field argument survives the four-keys-are-not-four-deaths correction, with the chosen option named and the surrounding PROSE checked for the implication that a timestamp correction marked an agent death
(C) fence parseability and the six member names confirmed by command

(D) MAJOR-2, MAJOR-3 and MAJOR-4 each confirmed closed on their merits, with §3's three exception pointers re-resolved individually against §4.1's text, and §2/§3/§4.1 re-read against each other for drift newly introduced by the 167-line rework
(E) the ORCHESTRATOR.md §7.2 count replacement checked for correctness AND for whether it repeats the growing-count defect
(F) scope confirmed: the ISS-0109 handoff untouched in 4101459, core-directives.md untouched, no issue/registry/log file touched by DOC-UPDATER
(G) confirmed that the four decisions, §5's scoping, and the append-only guarantees are unchanged
The verdict states the rework budget standing explicitly
No file outside this handoff is modified; `git status --porcelain` quoted

VERDICT: PASS. Re-derived from commit 4101459 and from the two doc files as they now stand, against the source handoff files themselves -- not from DOC-UPDATER's summary, not from ORCH's dispatch narrative, and NOT from my own Step 3b figures, one of which was itself wrong. My BLOCKER-1, MAJOR-1, MAJOR-2, MAJOR-3, MAJOR-4, MINOR-1 and MINOR-2 are all CLOSED on their merits. MINOR-3 is out of scope and filed as ISS-0195. Four NEW findings, all MINOR, none blocking -- listed in issues below as N1-N4.

FIRST, THE CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR FINDING. BLOCKER-1 proposed 'five death incidents across five runs, four of which improvised a key.' That figure was wrong and DOC-UPDATER was right to refuse it. I re-read all four `orch_*` VALUES myself (`python -c "json.load(...)"` over the four files, printing each key's value in full):
  - WF02-REQ023 `orch_timestamp_correction` -- verbatim: 'ORCH originally stamped created_at/started_at as 2026-08-16T19:08:00Z. That value was EXTRAPOLATED... Corrected to 2026-08-16T18:42:00Z'. ORCH correcting its OWN created_at/started_at -- fields section 3's table assigns to ORCH. NO AGENT DIED.
  - WF02-REQ037 `orch_timestamp_correction` -- verbatim: "SECURITY-REVIEWER's own completed_at read 2026-08-17T20:05:00Z, which postdates ORCH's real-clock check... Corrected here to the clock-plausible completion time". The agent completed and wrote its own result; ORCH corrected an implausible timestamp. NO AGENT DIED.
  - WF02-REQ027 `orch_restart_note` -- 'terminated mid-work by an infrastructure session limit'. DEATH.
  - WF03-ISS0109 `orch_reconstruction.reason` -- 'ELIXIR-DEV terminated on an API error after the merge landed and before writing result'. DEATH.
So two of the four keys are not death markers. My Step 3b figure inherited the Step 1 diagnosis's 'five' and re-emitted it inside a corrective finding -- the fourth-plus firing of docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source', this time carried by a GATE handoff. Recorded here plainly rather than glossed; DOC-UPDATER already reported it for an anti-patterns entry and ORCH is handling that, so I do not re-file it.

=== (A) BOTH TABLES RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY ===

SECTION 3's FOUR-ROW TABLE -- every cell PASSES. Command: `python` walking `glob.glob('handoffs/**/*.json', recursive=True)`, `json.load` on each, excluding registry.json, and for each file computing the top-level keys not in section 2's own schema set, together with each key's 1-based position, the file's key count, the Python type of the value, and the file's `completed_at`. The schema set was taken from section 2's fence itself (`json.loads` on the extracted fence -> 18 keys, minus `not_agent_attested` = 17), so the document supplies its own comparison set rather than my memory of it. 550 JSON files under handoffs/, 0 unparseable.
Measured, sorted by `completed_at`:
  2026-08-16T18:49:40Z | orch_timestamp_correction | WF02-REQ023-20260816/step-06-doc-updater.json                    | str  | pos 18/18
  2026-08-16T21:35:39Z | orch_restart_note         | WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02d-reviewer.json                       | str  | pos 18/18
  2026-08-17T19:45:30Z | orch_timestamp_correction | WF02-REQ037-20260817/step-02c-rework1-security-reviewer.json      | str  | pos 11/18
  2026-08-21T03:29:36Z | orch_reconstruction       | WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json                   | dict | pos 18/18
Every cell of the document's table matches: four key names in the right runs, four `completed_at` values byte-identical, shapes string/string/string/object, positions 18th/18, 18th/18, 11th/18, 18th/18. The derived aggregates in the prose beneath it -- four occurrences, four files, four runs, three names, two positions, two shapes, and '18th/last in three files, 11th/mid-file in one' in 4.1(b) -- all reproduce. The section-3 sentence assigning REQ027 and ISS0109 to death and the other two to timestamp correction reproduces against the values quoted above.
ONE DEFECT IN THE STATED METHOD, not in the figures -- see N1: the paragraph says the table was derived by 'json.load-ing every file under handoffs/ and subtracting section 2's own 17 schema keys'. Run literally, that procedure returns 26 occurrences in 13 files, not 4: it also picks up top-level `next_action` (5 files), `gate_history` (1), and 15 keys across the two flat-schema git-setup files. The additional filter actually applied -- keep the keys that record an out-of-band repair or correction, in practice the `orch_*` ones -- is stated semantically in the preceding sentence but not in the quoted procedure. A reader re-deriving as instructed gets 26 and concludes the table is wrong.

SECTION 4.1's THREE-DEATH COUNT -- PASSES, derived without reference to DOC-UPDATER's or my own prior figures. I did not start from the keys; I swept the run-level records for terminations and then checked each candidate.
  `grep -rniE "power outage|abnormal|api error|session limit|terminat" handoffs/registry.json handoffs/orchestrator.log` -> four candidate incidents in the 2026-08-16..21 window.
  1. WF02-REQ027 -- orchestrator.log:223 'RESTART ... Step 2d's first REVIEWER dispatch terminated mid-work by an infrastructure session limit', and registry.json:273 says the same at run level. Corroborates the handoff's own orch_restart_note. DEATH, treated by redispatch. Matches the table.
  2. WF02-REQ043 -- registry.json run note, verbatim: 'Interrupted by a host power outage mid-rebase (Step Final, reconciling against main after REQ-044 merged first); recovered in a later session.' Independently corroborated by docs/issues/ISS-0046.yaml, whose `discovered_in_run` is 'WF02-REQ043-20260818 (Step Final, resuming an interrupted prior session)' and whose body says 'interrupted prior session left the local feature branch mid-rebase against main'. Measured on the file: status 'PENDING', completed_at None, result None -- still untreated today. DEATH, treated by nothing. Matches the table.
  3. WF03-ISS0109 -- the orch_reconstruction.reason quoted above. DEATH, treated by ORCH reconstruction. Matches the table.
  4. WF02-REQ025-20260817 -- orchestrator.log:297: 'RESUME ... Resumed on hetzner-orch after prior session terminated abnormally mid-rework (uncommitted, incomplete edit to req025-event-append.md...)'. This is a FOURTH abnormal termination in the same window. It is genuinely OUTSIDE 4.1's class -- the session that died was ORCH's own, between dispatches, holding no agent handoff; ORCH resumed the same run and finished the edit in place, so no handoff result ever needed completing by a second party. The table's three rows are therefore the right three. But the sentence above the table is unbounded ('Three such deaths are on record, in three runs, between 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-21 -- essentially the whole recorded life of the pipeline'), and the sweep it invites turns up a fourth. See N2.
Three evidenced agent deaths CONFIRMED, each from a source independent of the amendment. The 'three incidents, three different treatments, one of which was no treatment at all' argument is sound and each treatment is verified above.

=== (B) DOES 4.1(b)'s ARGUMENT SURVIVE ITS OWN CORRECTION? RULING: YES -- OPTION (a), AND THE TEXT NOW SAYS THE FAMILY ===

I rule for option (a) of the three offered, and the reason is that the corrected text has already stopped arguing what the option-(c) objection assumes it argues. 4.1(b)'s required-field case is not 'there were N deaths'; it is 'when a writer needed to annotate a bookkeeping repair section 3's table gave it no slot for, it invented a key on the spot, four times, four ways, and the fourth silently changed shape'. That claim is about naming discipline, and every one of the four instances is a genuine instance of it, death or not. The family is real and section 3 now names it correctly: 'each run that hit a bookkeeping case the table did not cover improvised its own repair, in a non-schema top-level key invented on the spot' (line 270). Note the family is NOT 'ORCH wrote a field it does not own' -- WF02-REQ023 is ORCH correcting created_at/started_at, which section 3's table assigns to ORCH -- so 'a bookkeeping case the table did not cover' is the accurate and the chosen framing. Reconstruction is one member of that family; the field being specified marks that one member; the naming evidence generalises down to it cleanly. The argument holds as written.
THE BAR -- 'no reader should come away thinking orch_timestamp_correction marked an agent death'. I checked the prose, not the tables. It is met, and met redundantly:
  - Section 3, lines 283-286, states the split explicitly and by run id: 'Two of the four were written because the acting agent stopped existing (WF02-REQ027, an infrastructure session limit; WF03-ISS0109, an API error); the other two correct a timestamp, which is an adjacent case this table also failed to cover.'
  - Section 4.1, lines 354-357, states it again in the other direction and forbids the conflation by name: 'This is deliberately a smaller set than section 3's four ad-hoc keys, and the two must not be conflated: two of those four keys correct a timestamp rather than record a death, and WF02-REQ043 is a death that wrote no key all.'
  - 4.1(b)'s measurement paragraph does not assert death of any of the four; it defers to section 3's table by name ('section 3's table above is the measurement'), and that table's prose carries the split.
  - No sentence anywhere in either file attaches a death to WF02-REQ023 or WF02-REQ037. I checked every occurrence of both run ids and of `orch_timestamp_correction`.
RESIDUAL, MINOR, N4: 4.1(b)'s paragraph opens 'The convention was tried' and closes 'four agents each solving the same problem alone' without ever naming what the convention or the problem was, under a heading about a reconstruction marker. A reader entering at (b) is carried by the section heading, not by section 3's split. One clause naming the family in that first sentence would make the paragraph self-sufficient. This does not reach the bar above -- the paragraph explicitly sends the reader to section 3's table for the measurement -- so it is a precision improvement, not a defect.

=== (C) THE FENCE -- PASS ===
`python`: extract the first ```json fence from docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md by regex and `json.loads` it -> PARSES, 18 top-level keys: handoff_id, run_id, workflow_id, step, from_agent, to_agent, file, created_at, started_at, completed_at, status, priority, context, task, result, rework_count, max_rework, not_agent_attested. MAJOR-1 CLOSED -- the block parsed at 131aba9^, did not parse at 131aba9, and parses again at 4101459.
Member check, by command not by eye: `list(d['not_agent_attested'].keys())` -> ['reconstructed_by','reconstructed_at','reason','fields_written','evidence','not_verifiable_after_the_fact']. 4.1(b)'s table rows, read top to bottom: reconstructed_by, reconstructed_at, reason, fields_written, evidence, not_verifiable_after_the_fact. Identical, same order, no member in one and absent from the other.
THE EXPLANATORY TEXT WAS MOVED, NOT LOST -- and it gained. The deleted comment carried four assertions; the new prose beneath the fence (lines 134-152) carries all four and tightens one: OPTIONAL (kept, and sharpened to 'the one OPTIONAL field in the block above'), present only on a recovered handoff (kept and CORRECTED to '(a-2) only', with an explicit 'a 4.1(a-1) redispatch does NOT carry it' and a sentence saying that stamping it on a redispatched agent's report 'asserts the opposite of the truth' -- this is MINOR-1's fix, and it went further than MINOR-1 asked), absence carries meaning (kept, now flagged 'date-scoped' and pointed at (b)), see 4.1 for who may write it (kept). Added on top: a standing rule that the block must remain machine-parseable, why the placeholders are legal JSON, and that JSON has no comments so explanation goes in prose. That last rule is the durable fix -- it prevents MAJOR-1 recurring rather than only undoing it. Its forward reference resolves: the Enforcement note exists at the file's end and does name a linter (`tools/lint_handoffs.py` in R-Co, `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` as Letflow's gap).

=== (D) MAJOR-2 / MAJOR-3 / MAJOR-4 -- CLOSED ON THEIR MERITS, WITH ONE RESIDUAL ===

MAJOR-2 CLOSED. 4.1(a-2) now carries, in normative text: 'Exactly three fields are ORCH's to write here -- the same three section 3's table sends to this section, and no others', numbered `status`, `completed_at`, `result`, followed by 'All three MUST appear in (b)'s `fields_written`.' The headline sentence also changed from 'writes the result block' to 'completes the handoff', which is what removes the narrow reading. I re-resolved section 3's three pointers INDIVIDUALLY, each from the table row to the text it lands on:
  - row `completed_at` -> section 4.1 -> (a-2) item 2, which additionally forbids the two wrong values ('never an estimate of when the dead agent would have finished, and never back-dated to the side effect's own timestamp'). Lands on explicit normative text. This was the pointer that had no target; it now has the most specific one.
  - row `status` -> (a-2) item 1, 'to COMPLETED or FAILED, per section 4 step 1'. Lands.
  - row `result` -> (a-2)'s 'ORCH, and only ORCH, completes the handoff' plus item 3. Lands.
The weak-model failure mode MAJOR-2 named is closed by name in the same paragraph: 'Writing result alone and leaving status at PENDING with completed_at null is not a partial repair -- it reproduces exactly the defect the next paragraph rejects by measurement.' And the addition is bounded rather than open: 'started_at is not on this list and is not rewritten', which is the correct reading of section 3's 'ORCH only' row and stops the enumeration being read as general licence.
MAJOR-3 CLOSED, both halves plus the related clause. The parenthetical is now scoped to WF02-REQ043 alone (line 417). WF02-REQ062 gets its own paragraph headed 'ISS-0192's second file is NOT in this section's class, and must not be repaired under it', which reproduces ISS-0192's own reasoning and states the consequence I named: 'Applying (a-2) to it would stamp not_agent_attested onto a result that was agent-attested, asserting the precise falsehood the field exists to prevent.' I re-measured that file rather than trusting the amendment's 'Measured 2026-08-21': status 'PENDING', completed_at '2026-08-19T05:25:43Z', result present and non-null with result.status 'PASS'. Both cited values are exact. The paragraph closes with a usable discriminator -- 'A null result is what puts a handoff in this section's class; a bare PENDING is not' -- which is a better rule than the one I asked for, because it is checkable rather than case-by-case. The repair-time clause is present too, in (c) at lines 518-526, and resolves the REQ043-cited-on-both-sides tension explicitly, with the ancestry check re-verified.
MAJOR-4 CLOSED, with a boundary residual at N3. The absence claim is now date-scoped in its own headed paragraph: on or after 2026-08-21 absence asserts the result is the agent's own report; before that date 'absence asserts nothing... those files were never audited against a rule that did not exist'. The ISS-0109 file is named as the single authorised backfill, with the enumeration argument spelled out ('without this exception, the command offered below as the field's whole justification enumerates zero of the one reconstruction that exists, and does so permanently'), correctly characterised as a key rename over evidence already in the file, correctly NOT performed by this amendment, and correctly routed to the owning run. Both parts I said were needed are there.
RESIDUAL (N3): the boundary is day-granular and its own day contains the counter-example. Measured: 45 handoffs carry a `created_at` on 2026-08-21, of which 43 predate commit 131aba9 (committed 2026-08-21T12:13:08+05:00). One of the 43 is `handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json`, `created_at` 2026-08-21T03:24:18Z -- the repository's single genuine reconstruction, which carries no `not_agent_attested`. So as written, the rule asserts of that exact file that its result is the acting agent's own report. It is the file the same subsection names three paragraphs earlier, so a reader is warned, and the authorised backfill closes it -- but until that lands the sentence is false about 43 files including the one that matters most.
CROSS-SECTION DRIFT SWEEP OVER THE 167 CHANGED LINES -- NIL. I re-read section 2, section 3 and 4.1 against each other rather than each alone, in the direction the document declares authoritative. Fence members vs 4.1(b)'s table: identical (above). Section 2's prose modality vs 4.1(a-1)/(a-2): now agree, where they disagreed before. Section 3's three exception pointers vs 4.1(a-2)'s enumeration: agree, three for three. 4.1(b)'s `fields_written` example `["status","completed_at","result"]` vs (a-2)'s numbered list vs the authorised-backfill paragraph's `fields_written: ["status","completed_at","result"]`: all three restatements identical. 4.1(b)'s enum-violation figures vs the data: re-measured independently -- 13 files carry 'PASS' as a top-level status, 2 have no top-level status key, 0 other out-of-enum values, total 15. The rework made the 13/2 split explicit where 131aba9 stated only the 13, so the arithmetic is now shown rather than asserted. 4.1(d)'s cross-reference to ORCHESTRATOR 7.2 still resolves. No new contradiction introduced.

=== (E) THE UNSOLICITED 7.2 FIX -- PASS, AND IT DOES NOT REPEAT THE DEFECT ===
Correctness: `git show 131aba9:handoffs/registry.json | grep -c '"last_known_step"'` -> 62. The parenthetical claims exactly that, attributed to 'the commit that wrote 64' -- and 131aba9 is the commit that created 7.2 and wrote '64'. Verified exact, not approximately right.
The growing-count defect: NOT repeated, and the proof is already available. `grep -c '"last_known_step"' handoffs/registry.json` at HEAD -> 63. One commit later the figure has already moved, which is precisely MINOR-2's point, and the new text anticipates it in the sentence itself: 'The count grows with every run, so no fixed figure written into this file stays true; the point the sentence makes does not need one.' The NORMATIVE sentence now carries no figure at all -- 'Carried on nearly every run entry in handoffs/registry.json' -- and the surviving 62 sits inside a parenthetical explicitly bound to a named commit, which is a historical fact and cannot go stale. That is the right distinction and DOC-UPDATER drew it correctly.
I also checked the replacement's own claim rather than only its arithmetic: `json.load` over registry.json -> `runs` is a list of 63, and 63 of 63 carry `last_known_step`. 'Nearly every' is true and deliberately conservative for a file that grows. Same treatment applied to MINOR-2's own target: `grep -n "534\|64 times"` over both files -> no match, exit 1. The 534 headcount is gone and 4.1(b) says why in one parenthetical.

=== (F) SCOPE -- PASS ===
`git show --name-only --format= 4101459` -> exactly three paths: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md, docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03c-rework1.json. `handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json` does NOT appear -- the backfill is authorised in text and not performed, as required. No docs/issues/*.yaml, no registry.json, no orchestrator.log. `git diff 131aba9 4101459 -- docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md` -> 0 lines, so core-directives.md is untouched and MINOR-3 stayed out of scope; ISS-0195 exists untracked as ORCH's filing of it.

=== (G) NOTHING PASSING WAS DISTURBED -- PASS, BY HASH NOT BY EYE ===
For a 167-line rework I compared whole sections between revisions rather than reading them:
  HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md sections 5 through 7 (append-only, 'never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures', workspace hygiene): md5 455f0301f3af0fd8bce1c88e4c06209b at BOTH 131aba9 and 4101459 -- byte-identical.
  ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5 (the rework-counter scoping): md5 d3c80d4eb07ec47122ed09a8ce5a35b8 at both -- byte-identical, so the section-5 scoping I passed at Step 3b is exactly the text I passed.
  ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1 (re-read-before-write, no force push): md5 a4dba65f7de8d150e13fcd48dbe40d30 at both -- byte-identical.
  ORCHESTRATOR.md diff overall: 5 insertions, 2 deletions, one hunk, entirely inside 7.2's `last_known_step` paragraph.
The four ISS-0117 decisions are unchanged. 4.1(a-1) received no hunk at all. 4.1(d) received no hunk at all. (a-2)'s change is additive -- it enumerates three fields it already implied; it does not re-decide who may act. (b)'s decision (a required top-level field named exactly `not_agent_attested`, object, six named members) is unchanged and I verified the six against the fence. (c)'s probe-based discrimination is unchanged; the only insertion is the repair-time clause, which resolves an ambiguity rather than altering the predicate. Q1-Q4 remain decided as they were at Step 3b.
